newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans major Lanzhou oil refinery expansion.
newsitem.headline: China plans major Lanzhou oil refinery expansion.

text.p: China is planning to invest 3.82 billion yuan ($460 million) to expand the Lanzhou Oil Refinery in China's western Gansu province, an official at the refinery said on Tuesday.
The project, to be completed by 2003, would increase the firm's annual production capacity to 10 million tonnes from 5.5 million tonnes, the official told Reuters by telephone.
The crude oil used by the plant is mainly from oil fields in China's northwestern region of Xinjiang, the official said.

China has also begun building a railway linking Korla near existing oilfields in Xinjiang to Kashgar in the southern part of the region. The project calls for total investment of more than 6.0 billion yuan ($723 million), the Financial News said.
"If the railway in southern Xinjiang could be opened, it would be good for the transport of our crude oil," the official said without giving further details.
